content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket.

The employee is Ian Johnson (E028), requesting admin access to Payroll.

There are two notes in team memory:

Note 1 (from HR/ticket 1): role Payroll Specialist, employment type full_time, recommendation admin. Comment says full-time Payroll Specialist owns the Payroll system, so admin is within policy.

Note 2 (from Security/ticket 1): employment type contractor, security training basic, recommendation read. Comment says contractor with basic security training, contractors may have read, or write only with advanced training, never admin. The security database is authoritative.

So there's a conflict: HR says full-time, Security says contractor. The Security note explicitly says the security database is authoritative.

According to the policy:
1. full_time employees: up to write. Admin only if the employee's role owns the system.
2. contractor employees: read, or write if advanced security training. Never admin.

If full_time Payroll Specialist: admin allowed (role owns system). Requested admin = admin, grant admin.
If contractor with basic training: max read. Requested admin exceeds max, grant read.

Which to believe? The security note says their database is authoritative. The team memory says notes stay in shared memory, and the Approver reads the notes and makes the final decision. The Security agent says security database is authoritative (they looked it up). HR also looked up their own database.

The conflict: employment type differs. The security database says contractor. The security note claims authority on this. I need to decide.

Given the security agent's explicit statement that the security database is authoritative, and this is an access-level decision governed by employment type, I should treat the employee as a contractor with basic security training. Therefore max is read. Requested admin exceeds max, so grant read.

So decision: read.

Evidence: Security note (authoritative) shows contractor with basic security training, so contractor policy applies: never admin, max read without advanced training. Requested admin exceeds maximum, grant read.
